data.title: When third party claim may be filed
data.text:
A defendant or third party defendant may file a third party claim against another person who (a) is or might be liable to the party filing the third party claim for all or part of the claim against that party, (b) is or might be liable to the party filing the third party claim for an independent claim arising out of (i) a transaction or occurrence or series of transactions or occur- rences involved in the action between the plaintiff and the defendant, or (ii) a related transaction or occurrence or series of related trans- actions or occurrences, or (c) should be bound by a decision about an issue between the plaintiff and the defendant.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.44 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Form of third party claim
data.text:
A third party claim must (a) be in Form 16, (b) comply with the rules about pleadings in Part 13 [Technical Rules], Division 3 , [Pleadings]
(c) be filed and served on the plaintiff and the third party defendant, whether or not the third party defendant is already a party to the action, (i) within 6 months after the date on which the defendant filed a statement of defence or demand for notice, and (ii) before judgment is entered against the defendant or the defendant is noted in default, and (d) be accompanied, when it is served on the third party defendant, with a copy of the statement of claim served on the defendant.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.45 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

commentary.text:
This rule sets out the form required and the fact that third party claims must comply with the rules about pleadings in Part 13, Division 3. A third party claim is to be drafted as any other pleading, including setting out the facts necessary to establish a valid claim.
Time Limitation to File – There is a time limitation to file and serve a third party claim, being six months after the date on which the defendant (the party issuing the third party claim) filed a statement of defence or a demand for notice and before judgment is entered against the defendant or the defendant is noted in default. The case law informs the application of this six-month limitation.
Extension of Deadline – Key factors in considering whether to grant an extension are whether there has been inordinate delay, no credible or reasonable excuse and prejudice. H2 Canmore Apartments LP v. Cormode & Dickson Construction Edmonton Ltd., [2024] A.J. No. 903, 2024 ABKB 428 at paras. 20-21 (Alta. K.B.); Condominium Plan 9812082 v. Battistella Developments Inc.,[2014] A.J. No. 1167, 2014 ABQB 644 at para. 15 (Alta. Q.B.).
An additional factor may be whether the proposed third party claim has merit, which involves a low threshold sometimes described as “air of reality”. H2 Canmore Apartments LP v. Cormode & Dickson Construction Edmonton Ltd., [2024] A.J. No. 903, 2024 ABKB 428 at paras. 23-24 (Alta. K.B.); , Condominium Corp. No. 9813678 v. Statesman Corp.
Where the delay in advancing a third party claim is short, the primary focus of the application is on the excuse offered and the prejudice suffered. The requirement to explain the delay [2008] A.J. No. 904, 2008 ABQB 495 at para. 46 (Alta. Q.B.).

data.title: Third party defendant becomes party
data.text:
(1) On service of a third party claim, (a) the third party defendant becomes a party to the action between the plaintiff and the defendant, and (b) all subsequent proceedings in the action must name the third party as a party in the action between the plaintiff and the defendant.
(2) The pleadings between (a) the defendant and the third party defendant, and (b) a third party plaintiff and a third party defendant, form part of the court file between the plaintiff and the defendant.
(3) A third party claim must be tried with the other claims in the action unless the Court otherwise orders under rule 3.71 .
[Separating claims]

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.46 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Third party defendant’s options
sentences: A third party defendant may do one or more of the following:
(a) apply to the Court to set aside service in accordance with rule 11.31 [Setting aside service]
(b) apply to the Court for an order under rule 3.68 [Court options to deal with significant deficiencies] with respect to the third party claim
(c) apply to the Court for an order under rule 3.68 [Court options to deal with significant deficiencies] with respect to the plaintiff’s statement of claim
(d) file a statement of defence or demand for notice. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.47 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

commentary.text: Similar to rule 3.30, applying to a defendant served with a statement of claim, rule 3.47 summarizes the options available to third party defendants.

data.title: Plaintiff’s options
data.text:
A plaintiff in an action in which a third party claim is filed may apply to the Court for an order under rule 3.68 [Court options to deal with significant deficiencies] with respect to the third party claim.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.48 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Demand for notice by third party defendant
data.text:
(1) A demand for notice by a third party defendant must be in Form 18.
(2) If a third party defendant files a demand for notice, the third party defendant must file it and serve it on each of the other parties within the applicable time after service of the third party claim on the third party defendant.
(3) The applicable time is (a) 20 days if service is effected in Alberta, (b) one month if service is effected outside Alberta but in Canada, and (c) 2 months if service is effected outside Canada.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.50 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Judgment against third party defendant
data.text:
(1) The Court may give judgment against a third party defendant if the third party defendant does not file a statement of defence.
(2) Judgment against a defendant must be satisfied before judgment is enforced against a third party defendant unless the Court otherwise orders.
(3) An application by a defendant to enforce a judgment against a third party defendant under subrule (2) must (a) be in Form 19, and (b) be served on the plaintiff and the third party defendant.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.53 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Plaintiff’s reply to third party defence
data.text:
(1) A plaintiff or third party plaintiff may file a reply to a statement of defence filed by a third party defendant.
(2) If a plaintiff or third party plaintiff files a reply, the reply must (a) be in Form 20, (b) comply with the rules about pleadings in Part 13 [Technical Rules], Division 3 , and [Pleadings]
(c) be filed and served on the third party defendant and each of the other parties within 10 days after service of the statement of defence by the third party defendant on the plaintiff.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.54 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

commentary.text: Importantly, the plaintiff or third party plaintiff may reply to a statement of defence filed by a third party defendant. This is important in cases where the third party has defended the third party claim by denying the defendant’s liability to the plaintiff. The plaintiff has the right to respond to the third party’s pleadings about why the defendant is not liable to the plaintiff.

data.title: Application of rules to third party claims
data.text:
Except when the context or these rules otherwise provide, a rule that applies to or in respect of (a) a plaintiff applies equally to or in respect of a third party plaintiff, (b) a defendant applies equally to or in respect of a third party defendant, and (c) a pleading related to a claim made by a statement of claim applies equally to or in respect of a pleading related to a third party claim.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.55 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Status of counterclaim
data.text:
A counterclaim is an independent action.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.58 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*
sentences: A counterclaim is an independent action. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.58 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

commentary.text:
Rule 3.58 states that a counterclaim is an independent action. However, in practice although not reflected expressly in the , they are tied together more Rules of Court closely than two separate actions. Where there is a claim and counterclaim the parties hold concurrent questioning and set the matter down for trial concurrently, without the necessity of an order which would be required for two entirely separate actions. Omega Developments Inc. v. Canada Safeway Ltd., [2012] A.J. No. 967, 2012 ABQB 564 at para. 6 (Alta. Q.B. (Master)); see also, , [2016] A.J. No. 549, 2016 ABQB 172 WestJet v. ELS Marketing Inc. at para. 42 (Alta. Q.B.).
The settlement of the statement of claim or obtaining judgment on the statement of claim in an action does not settle or otherwise resolve the issues set out in the counterclaim which must be determined on their own. Richardson v. Richardson, [2018] A.J. No. 1177, 2018 ABCA 327 at para. 10 (Alta. C.A.). This is more important in the settlement context than the trial context, as the matters are usually heard at the same time.
One of the consequences of the counterclaim being an independent action is that a plaintiff might obtain summary judgment against the defendant on the plaintiff’s claim, even though the defendant’s counterclaim remains outstanding, Soler & Palau Canada Inc. v. Meyer’s Sheet Metal Ltd., [2012] A.J. No. 819, 2012 ABQB 496 at para. 47 (Alta. Q.B. (Master)); see also, , [2014] A.J. Bernum Petroleum Ltd. v. Birch Lake Energy Inc. No. 1199, 2014 ABQB 652 at para. 115 (Alta. Q.B.). or summary judgment on a counter- claim might be granted even though portions of the main claim must go to trial. Attila Dogan Construction and Installation Co. v. AMEC Americas Ltd., [2015] A.J. No. 1419,

data.title: Claiming set-off
data.text:
A matter that might be claimed by set-off may be claimed by counterclaim or by pleading set-off as a defence.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.59 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*
sentences: A matter that might be claimed by set-off may be claimed by counterclaim or by pleading set-off as a defence. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.59 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

commentary.text: It is not required to bring a counterclaim seeking set-off as a result of this rule. Set-off can now be pleaded as a defence. This eliminates the need for the issuance of a counterclaim which would only seek set-off, as was required under Former Rules 93(2). Tesla Exploration Ltd. v. Encana Corp., [2018] A.J. No. 451, 2018 ABQB 286 at para. 18 (Alta. Q.B.). Where set-off is pleaded as a defence, and the set-off amount exceeds the value of the plaintiff’s claim, no judgment can be entered for the defendant.A positive claim for set-off

data.title: Application of rules to counterclaims
data.text:
(1) Except when the context or these rules otherwise provide, a rule that applies to or in respect of (a) a plaintiff applies equally to or in respect of a plaintiff-by- counterclaim and a third party plaintiff-by-counterclaim, (b) a defendant applies equally to or in respect of a defendant-by- counterclaim and a third party defendant-by-counterclaim, and (c) a pleading related to a claim made by statement of claim applies equally to or in respect of a pleading related to a counterclaim.
(2) If the defendant-by-counterclaim does not file a statement of defence or demand for notice in respect of a counterclaim, a judgment on the counterclaim may be obtained only with the Court’s permission after notice of the applica- tion has been served on the defendant-by-counterclaim.

rules.title: Request for particulars
rules.text:
(1) A party on whom a pleading is served may serve on the party who served the pleading a request for particulars about anything in the pleading.

(3) If the Court orders particulars to be provided, it must specify a time within which the order is to be complied with.

rules.title: Identifying amendments to pleadings
rules.text:
(1) Unless the Court otherwise orders, if a party amends a pleading, a new pleading must be filed, being a copy of the original pleading as amended.
(2) The amendment must (a) be dated and identified, and each amended version must be identified, and (b) be endorsed by the court clerk in the following form:
Amended on [date] by [order] [party consent]
Dated . . .

commentary.text: There is no specific rule or authority governing the identification of amendments in pleadings. It was once common to use underlining (red for the first amendment, then green, and various other colours for subsequent amendments). The most common contemporary practice, acceptable to the clerks, is single underlining for first amendments, double underlining for second amendments and dotted-line underlining for third amendments, with no need to use different colours, or any particular colours, though colours are often used in conjunction with this practice.

rules.title: Time limit for application to disallow amendment to pleading
rules.text:
(1) On application, the Court may disallow an amendment to a pleading or a part of it.
(2) The application must be filed within 10 days after service on the applicant

rules.title: Permission of Court to amendment before or after close of pleadings
rules.text:
(1) Subject to subrule (5), before or after close of pleadings, the Court may give permission to amend a pleading.
(2) If the Court gives permission for a pleading to be amended, the Court must specify the time period within which the amended pleading must be filed and served.
(3) An order giving permission to amend a pleading under this rule ceases to have effect unless the amended pleading is filed and served within the time specified by the Court.
(4) If the Court directs or allows a pleading to be amended at trial, (a) the amendment must be recorded in writing by the court clerk, and (b) no order need be filed.
(5) This rule does not apply to an amendment to a pleading to add, remove, substitute or correct the name of a party to which rule 3.74 [Adding, removing or substituting parties after close of pleadings] applies.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.65 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

rules.title: Costs
rules.text:
(1) Subject to subrule (2), the costs, if any, as a result of an amendment to a pleading are to be borne by the party filing the amendment unless (a) the amendment is a response to an amended pleading, or (b) the Court otherwise orders.
(2) The costs of a contested application to amend a pleading are in the discretion of the Court, in accordance with rule 10.29 [General rule for payment of litigation costs].

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.66 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010); Alta.*

commentary.text: In an application seeking leave to amend pleadings, costs are at the discretion of the court. When the pleading itself is actually amended, the costs as a result of an amendment are to be borne by the party filing the amendment unless the party is responding to an amended pleading with an amendment or the court otherwise orders. “As a general rule where one party asserts a right to amend pleadings and the other party denies that right, and the amending party must take the matter to court, costs should follow the event. It [ ] the applicant succeeds in its motion to amend, it should get costs.” sic
